paper_title: AttentionInfluence Adopting Attention Head Influence for Weak-to-Strong   Pretraining Data Selection
caption: The statistics of clustering. The left is the clustering result of AttentionInfluence, the right part is that of FineWeb-Edu Classifier.
model_annotation: This figure presents two side-by-side pie charts comparing clustering results between the AttentionInfluence method (left) and the FineWeb-Edu Classifier (right), each displaying the distribution of content across multiple topic categories. Both charts use a two-tier (sunburst-style) structure, with an inner ring showing broader groupings and an outer ring showing finer subcategories, with numerical values (likely percentages) labeled alongside each category name. The left chart (AttentionInfluence) contains approximately 20 categories, with the largest slices being Education at 25 (shown in green), History & Society at 23 (shown in orange), Health & Medicine at 22 (shown in blue), Teaching & resources at 15 (green), Science at 15 (pink/red), Animal & Plant at 13 (orange), Tech & Engineer at 12 (blue), Science & technology education at 10 (light green), Society & culture at 10 (orange), Diseases at 11 (blue), Historical review at 7 (orange), Events & people at 6 (orange), Medical at 6 (blue), Nutrition at 5 (light blue), Infor tech at 5 (green), Emerging tech at 4 (green), Fin & Law at 3 (blue), Materials at 3 (orange), Manage at 2 (green), Materials at 2 (orange), and Policy at 1 (green). The right chart (FineWeb-Edu Classifier) shows a notably different distribution, with Education being the dominant category at 38 (green), followed by Science & technology education at 19 (green), Health & Medicine at 19 (blue), History & Society at 19 (orange), Teaching & resources at 17 (green), Science at 15 (pink/red), Historical review at 12 (orange), Animal & Plant at 12 (blue), Diseases at 10 (light blue), Tech & Engineer at 8 (blue), Nutrition at 7 (light blue), Society & culture at 5 (orange), Emerging tech at 4 (green), Infor tech at 3 (green), Materials at 3 (blue), Events & people at 2 (orange), Medical at 2 (blue), Healthy education at 2 (green), Manage at 1 (green), and Materials at 1 (green). Both charts use color coding to group related categories, with greens representing education and technology-related topics, blues for health and engineering, oranges for history and society, and pinks/reds for science. Percentage labels are displayed outside the slices with leader lines pointing to the corresponding segments, particularly for smaller slices. The segments appear arranged by thematic grouping rather than strictly by size.
